SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
April 11, 1934. 5801
No. D
Date ____ / ____ / ____

DEMARÉE C. BESS

Demarée C. Bess, an American citizen, was born in
1893 at Kansas City, Missouri. In addition to
studying at a high school in his native town, he attended
and graduated from the Columbia University, Missouri.

He is reputed to have worked on various of the
Kansas City daily newspapers until 1920 when he became
connected with the Christian Science Monitor of Boston,
Mass. He apparently impressed his employers for in
1924 he came to China as the Far Eastern Correspondent
of the Monitor. He came from the U.S.A. to Shanghai
where he stayed from April 1924 until the middle of 1925
when he made a two year tour of Japan in the interest of
his paper.

In May 1927 he was ordered to Peiping by his
employers and it was in Peiping that he met the present
Mrs. Dorothy G. **〔此处转录不清〕**, a divorcee, who was at one time
the wife of Randall Gould, present Executive Editor of the
Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury.

Whilst in Peiping Bess made the acquaintance of and
became very intimate with Mr. **〔此处转录不清〕**, Soviet citizen and
representative of the **〔此处转录不清〕** in Peiping. Bess
is reputed to have worked in close co-operation with
Slepach in Manchuria and through him became acquainted
with V. Royer, at one time Shanghai representative of
Tass, and another radical named C. F. Glass, a British
subject, who is reputed to have been at one time connected
with H. Isaacs, an American citizen of pronounced
communist tendencies.

Bess and his wife left Peiping for Shanghai by rail
about April 20, 1932, and arrived in Shanghai on April 24,
and on arrival here both put up at the Metropole Hotel.

德马雷·C·贝斯

德马雷·C·贝斯（Demarée C. Bess），美国公民，1893年生于密苏里州堪萨斯城。除了在家乡的高中就读外，他还进入并毕业于密苏里州的哥伦比亚大学。

据称，他在堪萨斯城的各家日报工作，直至1920年受雇于马萨诸塞州波士顿的《基督教科学箴言报》。他显然给雇主留下了深刻印象，因此于1924年来华，担任该报的远东通讯员。他从美国来到上海，在此停留至1925年年中，随后为了报社的利益前往日本进行了为期两年的游历。

1927年5月，他受雇主之命前往北平。正是在北平，他结识了现在的多萝西·G·**〔此处转录不清〕**夫人，她是一位离异女士，曾一度是现任《上海晚邮报与水星报》执行编辑兰德尔·古尔德（Randall Gould）的妻子。

在北平期间，贝斯结识了**〔此处转录不清〕**先生并与之关系极为密切，后者是苏联公民，也是**〔此处转录不清〕**驻北平的代表。据称，贝斯在满洲与斯列帕奇（Slepach）密切合作，并通过他认识了V·罗耶尔（V. Royer），此人曾任塔斯社驻上海代表；以及另一位激进分子C·F·格拉斯（C. F. Glass），系英国臣民，据称曾一度与具有明显共产主义倾向的美国公民H·艾萨克斯（H. Isaacs）有联系。

贝斯及其妻子于1932年4月20日左右乘火车离开北平前往上海，并于4月24日抵达上海。抵达后，两人均入住大都会酒店。

On May 18, 1933, officers of the S.M.P. interviewed
Bess in the Metropole Hotel in connection with the
finding of his name and address in a room at No. 7
Quinsan Gardens occupied by Miss Ting Ling(丁玲) and
a male Chinese named Fung Pah Ming (馮伯明) alias
Manu Fung alias Fung Kwang Chi(馮光之), who posed as
her husband.

Bess stated, when questioned, that he was in receipt
of a monthly journal entitled "The China Peasant and
Labourers Correspondence", a "Red" publication recommended
to him as containing items of interest by Slepack and
it was probably in that connection that his name had
appeared.

It was apparent to the officers interviewing Bess
that he was possessed of a profound knowledge of Communism
and that he was well on his guard the whole time. He
admitted that he had sent copies of "The China Peasants
and Labourers Correspondence" to the Christian Science
Monitor and that certain articles contained in the
Correspondence had been reprinted by the Monitor.

Note When Bess mentioned "The China Peasants and
Labourers Correspondence" he was referring
to "The Chinese Workers Correspondence", a
copy of which addressed to him has recently
been seized.

（批：See file 7916）

Bess and his wife resided at the Metropole Hotel
until July 22, 1933, when they removed to No. 839 Avenue
Foch, the home of Mrs. A. Ellis. On August 28, 1933,
Bess applied for rooms in the Cathay Mansions stating
that he desired to take up occupancy as from October 1,
1933. Between August 28, 1933, and September 20, 1933,
he apparently received orders to proceed to Japan, for
on the latter date he took over the rooms at the Cathay
Mansions on behalf of his wife and proceeded on September
page_data.zh:
-2-

1933年5月18日，工部局警务处警官在大都会酒店讯问了贝斯，原因是昆山路花园7号的一间房间内发现了他的姓名和地址，该房间由丁玲（Ting Ling）和一名名叫馮伯明（Fung Pah Ming）的中国男子占用，馮伯明又名Manu Fung，又名馮光之（Fung Kwang Chi），自称是她的丈夫。

贝斯在接受询问时称，他收到一份名为《中国农民与劳工通讯》的月刊，这是一份“红色”刊物，由斯列帕克（Slepack）推荐给他，称其中包含有趣的内容，他的名字很可能就是因此出现的。

负责讯问贝斯的警官明显看出，他对共产主义有着深刻的了解，并且在整个过程中都保持高度警惕。他承认曾将《中国农民与劳工通讯》的副本寄给《基督教科学箴言报》，且该通讯中的某些文章已被《箴言报》转载。

注：当贝斯提到《中国农民与劳工通讯》时，他指的是《中国工人通讯》，最近查获了一份寄给他的该刊物副本。

（批：见档案 7916）

贝斯及其妻子在大都会酒店居住至1933年7月22日，随后搬至福煦路839号A·埃利斯（A. Ellis）夫人的住所。1933年8月28日，贝斯申请国泰公寓的房间，称希望自1933年10月1日起入住。在1933年8月28日至1933年9月20日期间，他显然接到了前往日本的命令，因为他在后者日期代其妻子接管了国泰公寓的房间，并于9月

page_data.en:
-3-

28 to Japan where he remained until November 4, 1933,
on which date he returned to Shanghai.

From November 4, 1933, the pair resided at the
Cathay Mansions until January 29 when they left Shanghai
for Moscow giving their address in that city as No. 15
Bousoglebsky Pereulok, Moscow, U.S.S.R.

Discreet enquiries regarding the local activities
of Bess show that he contributed occasional articles to
the Shanghai Times and the Shanghai Evening Post and
Mercury. The consensus of opinion regarding the
man is to the effect that he was tremendously interested
in his profession, but conservative and not likely to
dabble in any reactionary undertaking beyond procuring
copy for his paper.

His journey to Moscow is reputedly at the orders
of his employers who have sent him there to relieve a
man named Chamberlain who has been correspondent for the
Christian Science Monitor in Moscow for the past eight
years.

-3-

28日前往日本，在那里停留至1933年11月4日，并于当日返回上海。

从1933年11月4日起，两人居住在国泰公寓，直至1月29日离开上海前往莫斯科，他们在该市的地址为：苏联莫斯科，Bousoglebsky Pereulok街15号。

关于贝斯在当地活动的谨慎调查显示，他偶尔向《字林西报》和《上海晚邮报与水星报》投稿。人们对他的普遍看法是，他对自己的职业极其感兴趣，但立场保守，不太可能涉足除为报社获取稿件以外的任何反动活动。

据称，他的莫斯科之行是奉雇主之命，派往那里接替一名叫张伯伦（Chamberlain）的人，此人在过去八年中一直担任《基督教科学箴言报》驻莫斯科的通讯员。
